subject: English_grammar
text:
Possessive adjectives
Possessive adjectives are words that go before nouns to talk about-
e belongings: | want to complete my homework first.
e —_ relationship: Mahin says that his mother is a banker.
e —_ parts of the body: Rimu has broken her leg.
e _ things that are connected with us: We have planted fifty coconut trees
in our school.
In the above examples, ‘my’, ‘his’, ‘her’ and ‘our’ are possessive pronouns
because they show possession.

Possessive pronoun
e We use possessive pronoun to talk about something that belongs to us
or is connected with us. It is usually used at the end of a sentence and is
not followed by a noun.
e We also use a possessive pronoun for the thing we are referring to. We
have already mentioned the thing in an earlier sentence.
